day1_consultation01.presenting_complaint: I've been having really bad diarrhea for the last 3 days
day1_consultation01.note:
Subjective: The patient reports diarrhea for three days with frequent loose and watery stools, lower abdominal pain on the left side, weakness, shakiness, a temperature of around 3-4 days ago, vomiting that stopped, loss of appetite, and feeling weak. The patient ate at a Chinese restaurant four days ago. The patient is an accountant who works and lives with his wife and two children. He doesn't smoke or drink alcohol. He uses an inhaler for asthma which is well controlled. He has been going to work despite symptoms. He feels that the symptoms have affected his daily life, making him need to stay close to a toilet.
Objective: The patient reports diarrhea, abdominal pain on the left side, weakness and shakiness. The patient had vomiting at the start of the symptoms but it stopped. Patient has been drinking fluids. Patient is working. No blood in stool or vomit. No fever currently, but felt hot previously. Patient is not taking any other medications.
Assessment: Gastroenteritis (tummy bug) is suspected. Possible bacterial cause.
Plan: Conservative management: stay hydrated with fluids and electrolyte replacement if vomiting/diarrhea persists. Paracetamol for fever and weakness as needed up to four times a day for the first few days. Rest at work for 2-3 days if symptoms don't improve within 3-4 days. If symptoms persist, return for further evaluation (stool sample) in 3-4 days.

day1_consultation02.note:
Subjective: The patient reports itchy and sore skin on their chest, hands, arms, and legs for three days. The patient has had eczema before which was only on the arms but now it is also on the chest and hands. The patient used a steroid cream from the pharmacy last night but did not help. The patient tried antihistamines but they didn't work either. The patient mentions hiking as an activity that causes pain due to itching. Patient lives with flatmates, works at a pharmaceutical company, and drinks alcohol occasionally.
Objective: The patient has itchy and sore skin on the chest, hands, arms, and legs. Skin is dry and cracked in some areas. No bleeding or discharge from the skin. The patient denies any other symptoms such as fever or cough. Patient denies smoking and drinking heavily. Patient reports using a steroid cream at the pharmacy last night.
Assessment: Eczema flare-up
Plan: Prescribe stronger steroid cream, prescribe emollients for bathing and showering, prescribe loratidine (antihistamine), advise patient to keep a diary of triggers, schedule follow-up appointment next week if symptoms don't improve. Suggests the patient try using the prescribed medications regularly for 7-10 days before deciding on further treatment.

day1_consultation03.note:
Subjective: The patient reports a terrible headache on the left side since midday. The patient mentions zigzag lines in her vision before the headache started. The patient feels nauseous and has vomited twice today. The patient states she is worried about brain cancer due to family history. The patient takes microgynon pills.
Objective: Patient reports headache on the left side. Patient reports zigzag lines in vision. Patient reports blurry vision. Patient reports nausea and vomiting. Patient denies fever or skin rashes. Patient denies neurological deficits such as speech problems, arm/leg weakness, balance issues, or injury. Patient reports being sensitive to bright lights. Patient reports headaches are throbbing and move with head movement. Patient reports no prior similar headaches. Patient reports stress at work. Patient lives alone. Patient does not smoke or drink alcohol. Patient reports no medications other than oral contraceptives.
Assessment: Not stated
Plan: Prescribe paracetamol or cocodamol for headache relief. Prescribe ibuprofen and naproxen for anti-inflammatory effects. Advise keeping a headache diary. Recommend follow up appointment in two to three days if symptoms worsen or do not improve. Instruct patient to return immediately if neck pain worsens, develops weakness in arms/legs, or visual changes occur. Provide advice regarding migraine management options (prophylactic medications) for persistent headaches.

day1_consultation04.presenting_complaint: I don't feel well, I have a cough and runny nose
day1_consultation04.note:
Subjective: The patient reports feeling under the weather for four days with sore throat, runny nose, cough, fatigue, night sweats, and mild fever that has subsided. The patient took paracetamol and ibuprofen which helped. There is some windedness on exertion. Muscle pain started a few days ago.
Objective: No abnormal white spots in the back of the throat. Clear nasal discharge. Dry cough. Mild shortness of breath on exertion. No chest pain. No ear problems or discharge. No headaches, vision changes, nausea, vomiting, bowel issues, or skin rashes. Family history of diabetes and eczema. The patient is otherwise healthy.
Assessment: Viral upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) with possible early signs of influenza. Not stated
Plan: Advised the patient to rest for a day or two if possible. Encourage hydration. Continue paracetamol and ibuprofen as needed. Return if symptoms worsen, high fever, labored breathing, or chest pain.

day1_consultation05.note:
Subjective: The patient reports lower abdominal pain, described as burning and getting worse over two days. The patient also reports feeling hot and sweaty. The patient had constipation last week but is now having normal bowel movements. The patient has noticed pink urine but denies any burning or stinging when urinating. The patient feels nauseous. The patient is sexually active with the same partner, who was last active four days ago. The patient uses an Implanon implant for contraception and has no other known medical history. The patient reports feeling well otherwise.
Objective: The patient's temperature is not mentioned. No other objective findings are provided in the transcript. Urine color is pink but no burning or stinging reported during urination. Bowel movements are normal. Patient denies fever, vomiting, shortness of breath, headaches, or vision problems. The patient reports being sexually active with a partner who was last active four days ago and uses an Implanon implant.
Assessment: Not stated
Plan: The clinician recommends empirically treating the patient for possible urinary tract infection (UTI) with Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole (Bactrim). The clinician advises the patient to take two tablets twice a day for three days. The clinician suggests that the patient also consider a pregnancy test, given her symptoms and use of an Implanon implant. The clinician recommends that the patient return if symptoms worsen or do not improve within a few days. The clinician advises the patient to take paracetamol for pain relief and drink plenty of fluids. The clinician sends a prescription for Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole to the patient's pharmacy.

day1_consultation06.note:
Subjective: The patient reports shortness of breath, worsening over the last couple of weeks. The patient feels breathless on minimal exertion and has a dry cough with some ankle swelling (bilateral). Patient denies chest pain or palpitations. Patient is feeling run down but otherwise normal. Patient has a history of heart failure and a small heart attack 5 years ago. Patient takes ferosimide, aspirin, simvastatin, and metaprolol. The patient denies allergies. Family history includes father with heart attack (died in his early 60s). Patient lives alone with two cats. Patient works part-time as a lorry driver during the day. Patient reports feeling more breathless even walking to the shops. Patient feels like she is getting worse and worries about her ability to work.
Objective: Patient has no chest pain, palpitations or dizziness. Heart rate is normal. Oxygen saturation is good. Blood pressure is normal. Ankle swelling noted bilaterally. No fever or signs of infection. Patient denies any other symptoms. Patient reports being able to pass urine normally and having a good appetite.
Assessment: Possible heart failure exacerbation. Further investigation needed to assess cardiac function.
Plan: Increase furosemide dose from one tablet daily to two tablets daily for the first few days. Order blood tests (full blood count, kidney function). Arrange echocardiogram of the heart. Follow up in one week to review symptoms and test results. Advise patient to call sooner if symptoms worsen or new symptoms develop.

day1_consultation07.presenting_complaint: I have a cough and cold
day1_consultation07.note:

The patient is supporting Partick Thistle and has been drinking alcohol (4-5 pints per week) and smoking occasionally. Patient lives with his wife.
Objective: Patient reports dry cough, runny nose, sore throat, mild ear discomfort, shortness of breath, and occasional fever/sweating. No chest pain reported. Patient denies any other significant complaints. Blood pressure slightly elevated. Patient takes metformine and Ryl. Patient reports being on a diet due to weight gain.
Assessment: Viral illness likely. Possible signs of flu or upper respiratory infection. Mild shortness of breath. Elevated blood pressure.
Plan: Advised to stay rested and drink fluids. Paracetamol recommended if needed for fever/ache. Antibiotics prescribed for possible bacterial superinfection if symptoms worsen after 24-48 hours. Follow up in one week if symptoms persist. Encourage quitting smoking.

day1_consultation09.note:

Examination findings are not stated. Urine analysis is not stated. Urinalysis was not performed. The patient denies any other symptoms like nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.
Assessment: Simple UTI/bladder infection
Plan: Prescribed Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim for a three-day course (one tablet twice daily). Advised to drink plenty of fluids and consider cranberry juice. Instructed the patient to call back if symptoms worsen or if she develops fever or back pain, indicating possible kidney involvement. Advised barrier contraception use.

day1_consultation11.note:
Subjective: The patient reports diarrhea, watery stools, frequent bowel movements (almost every hour), nausea, vomiting (occasional, especially with milk), mild abdominal cramps (in the middle), feeling hot, passing urine frequently, no blood in stool or throat, no family history of bowel problems, father has colon cancer (stage III), smokes socially, drinks beer occasionally (1-2 times per month), works at an office in central London (government). day1_consultation12.presenting_complaint: I've been having really bad diarrhoea for the last 3 days

She is not on any regular medications except for glasses since childhood. She denies allergies to medications. She socially smokes and drinks alcohol. The patient does not have any ideas as to what could be causing her symptoms. She wants stronger analgesia or painkillers.
Objective: Headache described as dull but sometimes sharper, located around the right eye and all over the head. It comes and goes, but is present most of the time. Light sensitivity reported. No vision loss or blurry vision. No neck pain or stiffness. Patient reports feeling sick with headache. Family history of migraines (mother and sister). Patient takes ibuprofen which did not help.
Assessment: Likely migraine headache given family history and symptoms. Not stated
Plan: Prescribe naproxen for pain relief. Advise patient to take up to two tablets three times a day. Recommend keeping a headache diary. Advise patient to return in one week if headaches worsen or are frequent. If vision loss, weakness in arms/legs, or other concerning symptoms, advise patient to call and return immediately.

day2_consultation02.presenting_complaint: I have a strange swelling on my elbow

The tip of the elbow is slightly dry. Patient denies eczema or other skin conditions. Patient has had blood tests done for inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatological antibodies, and gout.

Plan: Arrange blood tests to check for inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatological antibodies, and gout. Send blood test forms home with instructions. Arrange follow-up appointment via phone or video after blood test results are available. Advise patient to take ibuprofen 400mg twice daily after food if needed.
